events.title: Cypress open sourced
events.summary: Brian Mann open sourced [Cypress] on October 10, 2017 — a JavaScript end-to-end testing framework that runs inside the browser.
events.about: [Cypress] (`cy.visit`, `cy.get`, time-travel debugging) replaced flaky Selenium scripts for many front-end teams — tests run in the same event loop as the app. Real-time reloads and automatic waiting made E2E tests feel like unit tests for [React] and Vue SPAs.

narrative.whyChosen: [Cypress] made browser E2E testing developer-friendly after years of Selenium pain.
narrative.whyImportant: In-browser execution and auto-waiting set a new bar for front-end test reliability.
narrative.problemSolved: Selenium's remote WebDriver model was slow, flaky, and hard to debug for modern SPAs.

events.title: Google Pixel 2 released
events.summary: Google began selling the Google [Pixel] 2 — computational photography with Portrait Mode and Active Edge.
events.about: [Nexus] and [Pixel] phones were Google's pure-[Android] reference hardware for developers. Computational photography with portrait mode and active edge. [AOSP] builds and CTS testing often used [Pixel] devices as the baseline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Google [Pixel] 2 was a flagship Google [Android] reference device.
narrative.whyImportant: [Pixel]/[Nexus] hardware defines the reference [Android] experience for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed first-party reference phones without [OEM] skin fragmentation.
